title: Chapter 3 Quiz 14
description: Functions that call themselves, with factorial and Fibonacci.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is a **recursive** function?
options: A function that has no parameters
questions.explanation: Recursion is used when the definition of a concept refers to the same concept.

questions.question: In the factorial function, what is the **base case**?
questions.explanation: The base case stops the recursion. Without it the function would call itself forever.

questions.question: What is the **recursive case** of the factorial?
questions.explanation: Fact(N) = N × Fact(N-1) when N is not 0.

questions.question: Put the expansion of Fact(3) in order.
questions.explanation: The calls go down to the base case, then the results are multiplied back up.

questions.question: Complete the recursive factorial.
questions.code:
Function Fact(N : integer) Returns integer
Begin
    If N = {{1}} Then
        Fact ← 1
    Else
        Fact ← N * {{2}}
    EndIf
End Function
questions.explanation: The base case is N = 0. The recursive call must use a smaller value: N - 1.

questions.question: Fibonacci: F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1, F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2). Fill in the values.
questions.explanation: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21. Each term is the sum of the two before.

questions.question: Why is the simple recursive Fibonacci slow for large n (for example n > 30)?
options: It repeats the same calculations many times
It only works for even numbers
questions.explanation: F(n-1) and F(n-2) both recompute smaller terms again and again.

questions.question: What does **memoization** do?
options: It converts a function into a procedure
It stores computed results so they are not calculated again
questions.explanation: A table remembers results already found, which avoids recalculating.

questions.question: In the memoized Fibonacci, the table is first filled with {{1}} to mean 'not calculated yet'.
questions.explanation: If memo[n] is not -1, the stored result is returned directly.

questions.assertion: Memoization makes the recursive Fibonacci faster.
questions.reason: It stores the results already computed, so they are not calculated again.
questions.explanation: Both are true and the reason explains the speed-up: repeated work is removed.
